title: Sampling and roots
summary: Sampling let a server borrow the client's model and roots let a client tell a server which folders matter. Both are Deprecated in 2026-07-28 but still work, so know what they did and how to migrate.
useIf: You maintain a server or client that already uses them and need a migration plan before the earliest removal.
avoidIf: You are starting a new design. New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt either feature.

explain.md: **Sampling** (`sampling/createMessage`) lets a server ask the client's LLM for a completion. The request carries `messages`, `systemPrompt`, `maxTokens` and `modelPreferences`. Since 2025-11-25 a server can also pass `tools` and `toolChoice` if the client declares `sampling.tools`. The appeal was that the server needs no model key, and a human SHOULD be able to review and deny each request [[tr3]].

**Roots** (`roots/list`) let a client tell a server which directories and files it considers relevant. The spec says they are informational guidance, not access control: the protocol does not force a server to stay inside them [[tr4]].

In 2026-07-28 both are **Deprecated** (SEP-2577), together with Logging. They remain in the spec and still function, now carried by Multi Round-Trip Requests instead of server pushes. A deprecated feature stays at least twelve months, and the earliest removal is the first revision released on or after 2027-07-28. No feature has been Removed yet. Actual removal is a maintainer decision and may come later [[r9]] [[r25]].

explain.title: Read vendor dates carefully
explain.md: Microsoft Agent Framework documentation warns that sampling and `sampling_callback` are deprecated and says removal comes no later than 2027-07-28. That is stricter wording than the spec's earliest-removal date, so plan to the earlier one [[r26]].

pitfalls.symptom: A server read files outside the project the user opened
pitfalls.cause: Roots were treated as enforcement but they are only informational
pitfalls.fix: Enforce allowed base paths in the server and use OS-level sandboxing

pitfalls.symptom: A server upgrade breaks sampling in an old host
pitfalls.cause: The modern path sends sampling requests through Multi Round-Trip Requests, not pushed requests
pitfalls.fix: Keep the legacy transport path for hosts that still use `initialize`, and test both eras

pitfalls.symptom: A planned release assumes sampling will exist in 2028
pitfalls.cause: The earliest removal date was read as a guarantee
pitfalls.fix: Plan migration within the twelve-month window and watch the deprecated registry

scenarios.title: A new server that must summarise
scenarios.situation: A greenfield server stores meeting notes and must generate a stored summary for each one. The team can hold a model deployment and budget. Hosts vary.
constraints: Server needs its own stored artifact
unknowns: Is the summary cost billed to the server owner or the customer?
Which model deployment and gateway apply?
scenarios.question: How does the server get model output?

options.name: Call the model provider API from the server through a gateway
options.why: No dependence on a Deprecated feature or on a host that declares sampling, and you control prompts, cost and safety.
options.tradeoff: You own keys, spend and content-safety controls.

options.name: Return raw notes and let the host model summarise at read time
options.why: Needs no model access on the server.
options.tradeoff: No stored artifact and the result varies by host and model.

options.name: Use `sampling/createMessage`
options.why: New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it, and it only works with hosts that declare the sampling capability.
options.tradeoff: Reasonable only to keep an existing integration alive for legacy hosts.

flips.if: The server owner cannot hold model access and a customer's host supplies it
flips.then: Return data for the host model, since sampling is on its way out.

flips.if: Summaries are only needed ad hoc at read time
flips.then: Skip the stored artifact and let the host model summarise on demand.

scenarios.takeaway: Do not build on a feature that is already scheduled for removal.

scenarios.title: A shipped server using sampling
scenarios.situation: A server used by many customers relies on sampling for one feature. Some customers run older hosts and some run the 2026-07-28 revision. The current release window is a few months.
constraints: Removal is at least a year away
unknowns: How much traffic uses the feature?
scenarios.question: What do you do now?

options.name: Add a provider-API path, keep sampling for legacy hosts and set a retirement date
options.why: Avoids breaking customers while moving off the Deprecated feature inside the window.
options.tradeoff: Two code paths and extra testing until retirement.

options.name: Delete sampling immediately
options.why: Breaks hosts that rely on it for no benefit today.
options.tradeoff: Right once usage metrics show no legacy traffic.

options.name: Do nothing until removal is announced
options.tradeoff: Leaves migration to a deadline and risks an SDK dropping it earlier.

flips.if: Metrics show no legacy host uses the feature
An SDK you depend on announces earlier removal

scenarios.takeaway: Migrate on a schedule you control, with metrics deciding when the old path dies.

quiz.q: A server uses the client's roots as its only protection against reading outside a project. What is wrong?
options: Roots are informational and the protocol does not enforce them
quiz.explain: The spec calls roots guidance rather than access control. They are Deprecated, not Removed, and they are not tied to stdio or scopes. Enforce paths in the server.

flashcards.front: What is the status of sampling, roots and logging?
flashcards.back: Deprecated in 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577). Still functional. Earliest removal is the first revision released on or after 2027-07-28. Nothing is Removed yet.

flashcards.front: How should a server replace sampling?
flashcards.back: Call the model provider API directly (or return data for the host's model). New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt sampling.
No. They are informational guidance and the protocol does not enforce them. Enforce allowed paths in the server.
